note: The ambiguity corpus for issue #880. `declarations` is ordinary Kofun source, parsed by the same parser under test, so the signature environment every case resolves against is itself evidence that declaration external labels parse. Cases in `accept` state the surface kind, how many trailing lambdas attached, and the canonical text; cases in `reject` state the diagnostic category. Entries with "format": false say why they are not formatted.

declarationSurface.name: external label and internal name are distinct
declarationSurface.canonical: fn replace(in text: Text, from old: Text, to replacement: Text) -> Text

declarationSurface.name: ownership mode precedes the external label
declarationSurface.canonical: fn write(take into file: Int, bytes data: Int) -> Int

declarationSurface.name: a parameter without an external label is positional
a functional final parameter is what admits a trailing lambda
declarationSurface.canonical: fn fold(values: List[Int], initial start: Int, combine: (Int, Int) -> Int) -> Int

declarationSurface.name: a function type in domain position keeps its parentheses
declarationSurface.canonical: fn compose(outer: (Int -> Int) -> Int, thunk: () -> Int) -> Int

declarationSurface.name: an explicitly written read survives formatting
declarationSurface.canonical: fn keep(read value: Int, edit slot: Int, take thing: Int) -> Int

declarationSurface.name: an optional type and a functional final formal carrying one
declarationSurface.canonical: fn optional_bind(value: Bool?, next: Bool -> Bool?) -> Bool?

declarationSurface.name: a function hiding inside optional or moded keeps its parentheses
declarationSurface.canonical: fn nested(a: (Int?)?, b: take (Int -> Int) -> Int, c: List[(Int -> Int)?]) -> Int

declarationSurface.name: one terminal comma in a parameter list separates nothing (#1515)
declarationSurface.canonical: fn terminal(a: Int, b: Int) -> Int
